config.title: Build API gateway like proxy endpoint

intro.title: Build API gateway like proxy endpoint
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple API gateway-like proxy endpoint using Node.js. This proxy will forward incoming HTTP requests to another server and return the response, acting as an intermediary. You'll learn the core concept of HTTP proxying and how to handle request and response streams. The main technologies involved are the built-in Node.js 'http' module and the 'http-proxy' npm package. By the end, you'll have a working proxy server that can route traffic, which is a foundational skill for building scalable backend systems.
intro.usecase: API gateways are fundamental infrastructure in modern web applications, acting as a single entry point that routes requests to appropriate backend services. In e-commerce platforms, gateways handle product searches, shopping cart updates, and payment processing by directing requests to separate inventory, cart, and payment microservices. Content delivery networks use proxy endpoints to cache and distribute media files globally, reducing latency for users accessing videos or images. Developers implement these patterns when building dashboard applications that aggregate data from multiple APIs into unified interfaces for analytics or monitoring systems.

objectives: Construct a basic Express server to handle HTTP requests
Configure route handlers to intercept incoming API calls
Implement HTTP client functionality to forward requests to backend services
Manipulate request headers and parameters before proxying
Integrate response transformation logic for unified client output
Initialize error handling for failed proxy requests
Apply middleware to log proxy activities and monitor traffic

steps.title: Import required Node.js modules
steps.instruction: Import the http and https modules using require() statements.
steps.hint: Use require('module_name') to import Node.js core modules.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: importing a core module
const fs = require('fs');
steps.seedCode: // Import the http and https modules here
steps.expectedOutcome: The http and https modules are imported and available for use.
successCriteria: The http and https modules are imported using require() statements.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you import both the http and https modules using require().
steps.feedbackWrong: import both the http and https modules using require() statements.

steps.title: Create the main server function
steps.instruction: Create a function named 'createProxyServer' that initializes an HTTP server and listens on port 3000.
steps.hint: Use the http.createServer() method to create a server. Inside the function, call server.listen() with port 3000 and a console.log to indicate the server is running.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the http and https modules here

// Create the main server function here
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named createProxyServer that sets up an HTTP server listening on port 3000.
successCriteria: The createProxyServer function is defined, uses http.createServer(), and calls server.listen(3000) with a console.log callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the function, but make sure it includes http.createServer() and server.listen(3000) with a console.log callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function isn't set up correctly. Check that you're using http.createServer() and calling listen() on port 3000.

steps.title: Define the target API configuration
steps.instruction: Create a configuration object named 'targetConfig' with properties for the external API's hostname, port, and path.
steps.hint: Define an object with keys like 'hostname', 'port', and 'path' and assign appropriate string or number values.
steps.expectedOutcome: A 'targetConfig' object is defined with hostname, port, and path properties.
successCriteria: The 'targetConfig' object exists with 'hostname', 'port', and 'path' properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your 'targetConfig' object has all three required properties: hostname, port, and path.
steps.feedbackWrong: The configuration object isn't defined correctly. Create an object named 'targetConfig' with hostname, port, and path properties.

steps.title: Create the request handler function
steps.instruction: Create a function named handleRequest that will process incoming HTTP requests to your proxy server.
steps.hint: Define a function that takes request and response objects as parameters. You can use a function declaration or arrow function.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a function named handleRequest that's ready to process incoming HTTP requests.
successCriteria: A function named handleRequest is defined with req and res parameters.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've defined a function named handleRequest with both req and res parameters.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try creating a function named handleRequest that takes request and response parameters. This function will handle incoming HTTP requests.

steps.title: Parse incoming request details
steps.instruction: Inside your request handler function, extract the request method, headers, and path from the incoming request object.
steps.hint: Access the method, headers, and url properties from the request object. For the path, you'll need to parse the URL.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your request handler will have variables containing the method, headers, and path from the incoming request.
successCriteria: The request handler extracts the method, headers, and path from the request object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've extracted some details, but make sure to get the method, headers, and path from the request object.
steps.feedbackWrong: The request handler doesn't extract the required details. Check the request object properties.

steps.title: Set up the proxy request options
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, create an options object that will be used for the proxy request. Use the target API configuration (targetHost, targetPort, targetPath) and the incoming request details (method, headers, path).
steps.hint: The options object should have properties like hostname, port, path, method, and headers. Use the targetHost, targetPort, and targetPath variables for the hostname, port, and path respectively. Use the incoming request's method and headers for the method and headers.
steps.expectedOutcome: The requestHandler function now contains an options object that configures the proxy request to forward to the target API.
successCriteria: An options object is created inside requestHandler with properties hostname, port, path, method, and headers using the target API configuration and incoming request details.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started creating the options object, but make sure it includes all necessary properties: hostname, port, path, method, and headers.
steps.feedbackWrong: The options object is missing or incomplete. Remember to create an object with hostname, port, path, method, and headers properties using the target API configuration and incoming request details.

steps.title: Make the proxy request to the target API
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, use the https module to make a request to the target API with the configured options object. Store the result in a variable called proxyReq.
steps.hint: Use https.request() with the options object you created earlier. Remember to handle the response from the external API.
steps.expectedOutcome: The proxy request is initiated to forward the client's request to the external API.
successCriteria: The https.request() method is called with the options object and a callback function to handle the response.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using https.request() with the options object and storing it in a variable.
steps.feedbackWrong: The proxy request isn't set up correctly. Use https.request() with the options object to forward the request.

steps.title: Handle the target API response
steps.instruction: Inside the requestHandler function, add a callback to handle the response from the target API. This callback should receive the response from the target API and forward its status code, headers, and data to the original client response.
steps.hint: After making the proxy request, you can handle the response using a callback function that takes the target API's response as a parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The proxy request now has a callback that will process the response from the target API when it arrives.
successCriteria: The https.request call includes a callback function that receives proxyRes as a parameter and forwards the response to the original client.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the callback function is properly defined inside the https.request call and receives the proxyRes parameter.
steps.feedbackWrong: The response handler isn't set up correctly. Remember to add a callback function as the second argument to https.request that will handle the target API's response.

steps.title: Pipe the response back to the client
steps.instruction: Inside the proxy request callback, pipe the target API response data to the client response object.
steps.hint: Use the pipe method on the proxyRes object to forward the response to the client's res object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Forwarding a stream from one source to another
proxyRes.pipe(res);
steps.expectedOutcome: The target API's response data will be forwarded to the original client.
successCriteria: The proxyRes.pipe(res) method is called inside the proxy request callback.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're piping the proxyRes to the client's res object inside the callback.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires piping the target API response to the client response. Look at the analogous example for guidance.

steps.title: Start the server and test the proxy
steps.instruction: Start the server by calling the main server function to listen on port 3000 and log a startup message.
steps.hint: Use the .listen() method on the server object, passing the port number and a callback function that logs a message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to run on port 3000 and log a confirmation message when started.
successCriteria: The server is started using .listen() on port 3000 with a callback that logs a startup message.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the server, but make sure to include a callback that logs a message when it's listening.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly started. Check that you're calling .listen() with the correct port and a logging callback.
